name: Galileo
hook: The telescope, the moons of Jupiter and the Inquisition — Jeopardy's Renaissance astronomer.

facts.label: Pisa
facts.statement: Galileo was born in Pisa, where he became chair of mathematics in 1589 and whose airport is named for him.

facts.label: the telescope
facts.statement: Galileo did not invent the telescope — Hans Lippershey is credited with it in 1608 — but in 1609 he was first to turn it on the sky.

facts.label: the moons of Jupiter
facts.statement: In 1610 Galileo discovered the four largest moons of Jupiter and called them the Medicean stars; they are now called the Galilean satellites.

facts.label: the rings of Saturn
facts.statement: In 1610 Galileo became the first person to see the rings of Saturn.

facts.label: sunspots
facts.statement: Galileo was among the first to observe sunspots, dark solar regions that wax and wane in 11-year cycles.

facts.label: the Inquisition
facts.statement: The Inquisition summoned Galileo to Rome for promoting Copernicus's heliocentric ideas; in 1992 the Church admitted it had erred in condemning him.

facts.label: the hammer and feather experiment
facts.statement: On the Moon in 1971, an astronaut repeated Galileo's falling-body experiment and declared that Galileo "was correct."
